desc:
Compute the sum of the first n terms of the geometric sequence with first term 1 and ratio r:

S = 1 + r + r2 + ... + rn-1

Return S modulo 1,000,000,007, as a value in the range 0 .. 1,000,000,006. The true sum is far too large to compute directly.

r = 2, n = 10         -> 1023
r = 0, n = 5          -> 1   (the first term is 00 = 1)
r = 1000000008, n = 3 -> 3   (r is congruent to 1 modulo the prime)
hints: Split the sum in halves: the first 2m terms equal the first m terms plus r<sup>m</sup> times that same partial sum.
Recurse on n / 2 while tracking r<sup>n</sup> alongside the partial sum; this takes O(log n) multiplications.
Reduce r modulo 1,000,000,007 first, so that every intermediate value stays below the modulus.
editorial: Let S(k) be the sum of the first k terms and P(k) = rk. For even k = 2m, S(2m) = S(m) * (1 + P(m)) and P(2m) = P(m)2. For odd k, S(k) = S(k-1) + P(k-1) and P(k) = P(k-1) * r. Halving k computes both values in O(log n) multiplications, the same idea as fast exponentiation.

The closed form (rn - 1) / (r - 1) is tempting, but it needs a modular inverse and breaks when r is congruent to 1 modulo the prime, which the sample with r = 1000000008 exercises. The doubling recursion has no such special case.
